chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man leaves behind his father and mother, or his son or his daughter, if he leaves one of these four, they are not those whom Allah meant [by the term] 'Al-Kalalah' [in the verse]: 'Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning Kalalah.'

key_terms.ابْنَهُ أَوِ ابْنَتَهُ: His son or his daughter (direct descendants)
key_terms.الْكَلَالَةِ: Kalalah (one who leaves no direct ascendants or descendants)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalalah in Shia inheritance jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the definition of 'Al-Kalalah' is precisely narrowed to exclude cases where direct ascendants (parents) or descendants (children) survive, thereby distinguishing them from the specific inheritance rules for those with no direct lineage. This clarification is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the applicability of the detailed verses in Surah An-Nisa, ensuring that the presence of even one direct parent or child precludes the application of the Kalalah-specific distribution. This hadith serves as a key interpretive tool (tafsir) for understanding the scope of 'Kalalah' beyond the literal text of the Quran.
